items.followUp: State two uses of radioisotopes in medicine and one use in radiotherapy.

rubric.why: Identifies the isotope used in radiotherapy and its application.
rubric.description: Cobalt-60 emits gamma rays used to destroy cancer cells in radiotherapy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming cobalt-60 and 1 mark for its use against cancer.

rubric.why: Links iodine-131 to a medical use involving the thyroid.
rubric.description: Iodine-131 is used to diagnose or treat disorders of the thyroid gland.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking iodine-131 with the thyroid.

rubric.description: Sodium-24 is used as a radioactive tracer to study blood circulation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking sodium-24 with tracing blood circulation.

rubric.why: Identifies a medical treatment application of phosphorus-32.
rubric.description: Phosphorus-32 is used to treat some blood diseases, including leukemia.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking phosphorus-32 with leukemia or another blood disease.

modelAnswer: Cobalt-60 emits gamma rays that are used in radiotherapy to destroy cancer cells.
Iodine-131 is used to diagnose or treat disorders of the thyroid gland.
Sodium-24 is used as a radioactive tracer to study blood circulation.
Phosphorus-32 is used to treat some blood diseases, including leukemia.

items.followUp: Explain how a single covalent bond differs from a double covalent bond, giving an example of each.

rubric.why: Defines a covalent bond by the sharing of electron pairs between atoms.
rubric.description: A covalent bond forms when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a clear definition; award 1 mark if sharing is mentioned but the definition is incomplete.

rubric.why: A single covalent bond has one shared pair of electrons and H₂ is an example.
rubric.description: Explains the single covalent bond and gives H₂ as an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct description and example.

rubric.why: A double covalent bond has two shared pairs of electrons and O₂ is an example.
rubric.description: Explains the double covalent bond and gives O₂ as an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct description and example.

rubric.why: A triple covalent bond has three shared pairs of electrons and N₂ is an example.
rubric.description: Explains the triple covalent bond and gives N₂ as an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct description and example.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
A single covalent bond has one shared pair of electrons; an example is H₂.
A double covalent bond has two shared pairs of electrons; an example is O₂.
A triple covalent bond has three shared pairs of electrons; an example is N₂.

items.followUp: What are isotopes? Give two isotopes of hydrogen as an example.

rubric.why: States the defining similarity and difference between isotopes.
rubric.description: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both the same proton/atomic number and the different mass/neutron number.

rubric.why: Provides a correct example of isotopes of the same element.
rubric.description: Gives hydrogen-1 and hydrogen-2 as an example pair.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct pair of isotopes.

modelAnswer: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers; they have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Hydrogen-1 and hydrogen-2 are examples of isotopes.

items.followUp: Describe cathode rays and name the scientist who discovered them.

rubric.why: Identifies cathode rays as electrons travelling from the cathode.
rubric.description: Cathode rays are streams of electrons emitted from the cathode in a discharge tube.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing cathode rays as streams or rays of electrons.

rubric.why: Names William Crookes as the discoverer of cathode rays.
rubric.description: Cathode rays were discovered by William Crookes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming William Crookes.

modelAnswer: Cathode rays are streams of electrons emitted from the cathode in a discharge tube.
They were discovered by William Crookes.
